1.15.title: Disorders of the skeletal spine resulting in compromise of a nerve root(s)
1.15.summary: Spine disorder compressing a nerve root, with radicular symptoms, neurological signs on exam or electrodiagnostic testing, imaging confirmation in cervical or lumbosacral spine, and ≥12-month physical limitation requiring an assistive device or producing inability to use upper extremities.

children.criterion: Radicular distribution of symptoms consistent with nerve root compromise
Pain in radicular distribution consistent with nerve root compromise
Paresthesia in radicular distribution consistent with nerve root compromise
Muscle fatigue in radicular distribution consistent with nerve root compromise
Radicular neurological signs on physical examination or diagnostic test
Muscle weakness in a myotomal pattern documented on physical examination
Signs of nerve root irritation, tension, or compression on physical exam (e.g., positive straight leg raise, Spurling, Lasegue)
Sensory changes OR decreased deep tendon reflexes
Decreased sensation in radicular distribution on physical exam
Abnormal sensory nerve latency on electrodiagnostic testing (EMG/NCS)
Decreased deep tendon reflexes in radicular distribution
Imaging findings consistent with nerve root compromise in cervical or lumbosacral spine (e.g., disc herniation, foraminal stenosis on MRI/CT/myelogram)
Physical limitation lasting ≥12 months with documented assistive device need OR upper extremity inability
Impairment-related physical limitation of musculoskeletal functioning lasting or expected to last ≥12 continuous months
Documented medical need for two-handed assistive device OR limitation of one or both upper extremities
Documented medical need for walker, bilateral canes, bilateral crutches, or two-handed wheeled mobility device
Inability to use one upper extremity for fine and gross movements; needs one-handed assistive device requiring the other upper extremity
Inability to use either upper extremity for fine and gross movements (work-related activities)

1.16.title: Lumbar spinal stenosis resulting in compromise of the cauda equina
1.16.summary: Lumbar spinal stenosis with cauda equina compromise documented by A (neurological symptom), B (nonradicular neurological signs: muscle weakness and either sensory changes or decreased DTRs), C (imaging/operative findings), and D (≥12-month limitation with documented assistive device need).

children.criterion: Symptom(s) of neurological compromise manifested as A.1, A.2, or A.3
Nonradicular distribution of pain in one or both lower extremities
Nonradicular distribution of sensory loss in one or both lower extremities
Neurogenic claudication
Nonradicular neurological signs present during physical examination (see 1.00C2) or on a diagnostic test (see 1.00C3), evidenced by B.1 AND (B.2 OR B.3)
Muscle weakness on physical exam of lower extremities
Sensory changes (B.2) OR decreased deep tendon reflexes (B.3)
Sensory changes evidenced by B.2.a, B.2.b, or B.2.c
Decreased sensation
Sensory nerve deficit (abnormal sensory nerve latency) on electrodiagnostic testing
Areflexia, trophic ulceration, or bladder or bowel incontinence
Decreased deep tendon reflexes in one or both lower extremities
Findings on imaging (see 1.00C3) or in an operative report (see 1.00C4) consistent with compromise of the cauda equina with lumbar spinal stenosis

Impairment-related physical limitation of musculoskeletal functioning that has lasted, or is expected to last, for a continuous period of at least 12 months, AND medical documentation of at least one of D.1 or D.2
Documented medical need (see 1.00C6a) for a walker, bilateral canes, or bilateral crutches (see 1.00C6d), or a wheeled and seated mobility device involving the use of both hands (see 1.00C6e(i))

Inability to use one upper extremity to independently initiate, sustain, and complete work-related activities involving fine and gross movements (see 1.00E4), AND documented medical need (see 1.00C6a) for a one-handed, hand-held assistive device that requires the use of the other upper extremity, or a wheeled and seated mobility device involving the use of one hand (see 1.00C6e(ii))

1.17.title: Reconstructive surgery or surgical arthrodesis of a major weight-bearing joint
1.17.summary: Reconstructive surgery or arthrodesis of a major weight-bearing joint with impairment-related limitation lasting ≥12 months and documented need for two-handed assistive device.

children.criterion: Surgical reconstruction or arthrodesis of a major weight-bearing joint (hip, knee, ankle, or ankle-hindfoot complex)
Impairment-related physical limitation of musculoskeletal functioning that has lasted, or is expected to last, ≥12 months from the surgery
Documented medical need for walker, bilateral canes, bilateral crutches, or two-handed wheeled mobility device

1.18.title: Abnormality of a major joint(s) in any extremity
1.18.summary: Major joint abnormality documented by A (chronic joint pain or stiffness), B (abnormal motion, instability, or immobility), C (anatomical abnormality on exam or imaging), and D (≥12-month limitation with documented assistive device need or upper extremity inability).

children.criterion: Chronic joint pain or stiffness
Abnormal motion, instability, or immobility of the affected joint(s)
Anatomical abnormality of the affected joint(s) noted on C.1 or C.2
Physical examination (for example, subluxation, contracture, or bony or fibrous ankylosis)
Imaging (for example, joint space narrowing, bony destruction, or ankylosis or arthrodesis of the affected joint)

Impairment-related physical limitation of musculoskeletal functioning that has lasted, or is expected to last, for a continuous period of at least 12 months, AND medical documentation of at least one of D.1, D.2, or D.3
Documented medical need (see 1.00C6a) for a walker, bilateral canes, or bilateral crutches (see 1.00C6d), or a wheeled and seated mobility device involving the use of both hands (see 1.00C6e(i))

Inability to use one upper extremity to independently initiate, sustain, and complete work-related activities involving fine and gross movements (see 1.00E4), AND documented medical need (see 1.00C6a) for a one-handed, hand-held assistive device that requires the use of the other upper extremity, or a wheeled and seated mobility device involving the use of one hand (see 1.00C6e(ii))
Inability to use both upper extremities to the extent that neither can be used to independently initiate, sustain, and complete work-related activities involving fine and gross movements (see 1.00E4)

1.19.title: Pathologic fractures due to any cause
1.19.summary: Three pathologic fractures on separate occasions within a 12-month period (see 1.00J), AND impairment-related physical limitation lasting 12+ months with one of: walker/bilateral canes need, one-upper-extremity inability with one-handed device, or both-upper-extremities inability.

children.criterion: Three pathologic fractures occurring on separate, distinct occasions within a 12-month period (see 1.00J)
Impairment-related physical limitation of musculoskeletal functioning lasting 12+ months AND medical documentation of one of B.1, B.2, or B.3
Impairment-related physical limitation of musculoskeletal functioning that has lasted, or is expected to last, for at least 12 continuous months
One of: B.1 (walker/bilateral canes), B.2 (one upper extremity inability + one-handed device), B.3 (both upper extremities inability)
Documented medical need (see 1.00C6a) for a walker, bilateral canes, or bilateral crutches (see 1.00C6d), or a wheeled and seated mobility device involving the use of both hands (see 1.00C6e(i))

Inability to use one upper extremity to independently initiate, sustain, and complete work-related activities involving fine and gross movements (see 1.00E4), AND documented medical need for a one-handed, hand-held assistive device requiring the use of the other upper extremity, or a wheeled and seated mobility device involving the use of one hand (see 1.00C6e(ii))
Inability to use both upper extremities to the extent that neither can be used to independently initiate, sustain, and complete work-related activities involving fine and gross movements (see 1.00E4)

1.20.title: Amputation due to any cause
1.20.summary: Amputation that meets one of four scenarios: both upper extremities, hemipelvectomy/hip disarticulation, lower extremity at/above ankle precluding effective ambulation, or one hand and one lower extremity precluding effective ambulation.

children.criterion: Amputation of both upper extremities at or above the wrist
Hemipelvectomy or hip disarticulation
Amputation of one or both lower extremities at or above the ankle, with stump complications precluding effective prosthetic use, lasting ≥12 months
Amputation of one or both lower extremities at or above the ankle
Stump complications (non-healing wounds, ulceration, instability) preventing or precluding effective prosthetic use
Documented medical need for walker, bilateral canes, bilateral crutches, or two-handed wheeled mobility device
Amputation of one hand AND one lower extremity at or above the ankle, with two-handed assistive device need lasting ≥12 months
Amputation of one upper extremity at or above the wrist AND one lower extremity at or above the ankle
Documented medical need for walker, bilateral canes, bilateral crutches, or two-handed wheeled mobility device, lasting ≥12 months

1.21.title: Soft tissue injury or abnormality under continuing surgical management
1.21.summary: Soft tissue injury (including burns) under continuing surgical management directed at saving, reconstructing, or replacing the affected part, with continuing management expected to last ≥12 months and maximum benefit from therapy not yet achieved.

children.criterion: Soft tissue injury or abnormality of an extremity, trunk, or face/head requiring continuing surgical management
Continuing surgical management directed at saving, reconstructing, or replacing the affected body part
Continuing surgical management expected to last, or has lasted, ≥12 months from initial event, with maximum benefit from therapy not yet achieved

1.22.title: Non-healing or complex fracture of the femur, tibia, pelvis, or one or more of the tarsal bones
1.22.summary: Non-healing (nonunion) or complex fracture of femur, tibia, pelvis, or tarsal bones, imaging-confirmed, with limitation lasting ≥12 months and need for two-handed assistive device.

children.criterion: Non-healing (nonunion) or complex fracture of femur, tibia, pelvis, or one or more tarsal bones
Imaging documenting the non-healing or complex nature of the fracture
≥12-month physical limitation with documented two-handed assistive device need
Impairment-related physical limitation lasting or expected to last ≥12 continuous months
Documented medical need for walker, bilateral canes, bilateral crutches, or two-handed wheeled mobility device

1.23.title: Non-healing or complex fracture of an upper extremity
1.23.summary: Non-healing (nonunion) or complex fracture of an upper extremity (humerus, radius, or ulna) (see 1.00N), AND impairment-related limitation lasting 12+ months with inability to use both upper extremities for fine and gross movements.

children.criterion: Non-healing (nonunion) or complex fracture of an upper extremity (humerus, radius, or ulna) (see 1.00N), documented by imaging or operative report

Impairment-related physical limitation of musculoskeletal functioning that has lasted, or is expected to last, for at least 12 continuous months, AND medical documentation of the inability to use both upper extremities to the extent that neither can be used to independently initiate, sustain, and complete work-related activities involving fine and gross movements (see 1.00E4)

2.02.title: Loss of central visual acuity
2.02.summary: Best-corrected central visual acuity in the better eye of 20/200 or worse.

rule_json.criterion: Best-corrected central visual acuity in the better eye of 20/200 or worse, measured by ophthalmologist or optometrist

2.03.title: Contraction of the visual field in the better eye
2.03.summary: Contraction of visual field in the better eye meeting one of: widest diameter ≤20°, mean deviation worse than -22 dB, or visual field efficiency ≤20%.

children.criterion: Widest diameter of visual field in the better eye, subtending an angle around the point of fixation, no greater than 20°
Mean deviation (MD) of -22 dB or worse in the better eye on automated static threshold perimetry (HFA)
Visual field efficiency of 20% or less in the better eye

2.04.title: Visual impairment (combined acuity and field impairment)
2.04.summary: Loss of visual efficiency, or visual impairment, in the better eye. A) Visual efficiency percentage of 20 or less after best correction; or B) Visual impairment value of 1.00 or greater after best correction.

children.criterion: A visual efficiency percentage of 20 or less after best correction (see 2.00A7d). Calculated as: visual acuity efficiency percentage (2.00A7b) × visual field efficiency percentage (2.00A7c) ÷ 100, in the better eye.
A visual impairment value of 1.00 or greater after best correction (see 2.00A8d). Calculated as: visual acuity impairment value (2.00A8b) + visual field impairment value (2.00A8c), in the better eye.

2.07.title: Disturbance of labyrinthine-vestibular function
2.07.summary: Disturbance of labyrinthine-vestibular function (including Meniere's disease), characterized by a history of frequent attacks of balance disturbance, tinnitus, and progressive hearing loss, with BOTH A) disturbed vestibular function on caloric/other vestibular tests AND B) hearing loss established by audiometry.

children.criterion: Disturbance of labyrinthine-vestibular function (including Meniere's disease), characterized by a history of frequent attacks of balance disturbance, tinnitus, and progressive loss of hearing
Disturbed function of vestibular labyrinth demonstrated by caloric or other vestibular tests
Hearing loss established by audiometry

2.09.title: Loss of speech
2.09.summary: Loss of speech due to any cause, with inability to produce by any means speech that can be heard, understood, or sustained.

rule_json.criterion: Loss of speech due to any cause, with inability to produce — by any means — speech that can be heard, understood, or sustained

2.10.title: Hearing loss not treated with cochlear implantation
2.10.summary: Hearing loss in the better ear meeting one of: pure-tone average ≥90 dB AND bone conduction average ≥60 dB, OR word recognition score 40% or less.

children.criterion: Average air conduction hearing threshold of 90 decibels (dB) or greater in the better ear AND average bone conduction hearing threshold of 60 dB or greater in the better ear (at 500, 1000, and 2000 Hz)
Word recognition score of 40% or less in the better ear, determined using a standardized list of phonetically balanced monosyllabic words

2.11.title: Hearing loss treated with cochlear implantation
2.11.summary: Hearing loss treated with cochlear implantation; considered disabled for 1 year following implantation, after which evaluation is based on word recognition score on HINT (≤60% qualifies).

children.criterion: Within 1 year of cochlear implantation surgery (claimant considered disabled for 1 year)
After 1 year, word recognition score of 60% or less determined by HINT (Hearing in Noise Test)

3.02.title: Chronic respiratory disorders
3.02.summary: Chronic respiratory disorder due to any cause except CF, meeting one of: A FEV1 ≤ Table I-A/I-B value; B FVC ≤ Table II-A/II-B value; C chronic impairment of gas exchange (C.1 DLCO ≤ Table III, C.2 ABG PaO2/PaCO2 ≤ Table IV-A/B/C, or C.3 SpO2 ≤ Table V); or D exacerbations/complications requiring three hospitalizations within a 12-month period, each lasting ≥48 hours and at least 30 days apart.

children.criterion: FEV1 (see 3.00E) less than or equal to the value in Table I-A or I-B for age, gender, and height without shoes (see 3.00E3a)
FVC (see 3.00E) less than or equal to the value in Table II-A or II-B for age, gender, and height without shoes (see 3.00E3a)
Chronic impairment of gas exchange demonstrated by C.1, C.2, or C.3
Average of two unadjusted, single-breath DLCO measurements (see 3.00F) less than or equal to the value in Table III for gender and height without shoes (see 3.00F3a)

Arterial PaO2 and PaCO2 measured concurrently by an ABG test, at rest or during steady state exercise, breathing room air (see 3.00G3b), less than or equal to the applicable values in Table IV-A, IV-B, or IV-C
SpO2 measured by pulse oximetry (see 3.00H2) either at rest, during a 6MWT, or after a 6MWT, less than or equal to the value in Table V

Exacerbations or complications requiring three hospitalizations within a 12-month period and at least 30 days apart (the 12-month period must occur within the period we are considering in connection with your application or continuing disability review). Each hospitalization must last at least 48 hours, including hours in a hospital emergency department immediately before the hospitalization.

3.03.title: Asthma
3.03.summary: Asthma with low FEV1 at baseline AND three asthma exacerbations within a 12-month period requiring hospitalization for ≥48 hours, despite prescribed treatment.

children.criterion: Baseline FEV1 less than or equal to the value in SSA Table VI-A or VI-B for age, sex, and height, measured while medically stable, within the same 12-month period as required hospitalizations

Three asthma exacerbations within a consecutive 12-month period requiring hospitalization for at least 48 hours each, with at least 30 days between consecutive hospitalizations, despite adherence to prescribed treatment

3.04.title: Cystic fibrosis
3.04.summary: Cystic fibrosis (documented per 3.00J2) meeting one of: A FEV1 ≤ Table VII-A/VII-B value; B three hospitalizations within a 12-month period ≥30 days apart; C spontaneous pneumothorax requiring chest tube; D respiratory failure requiring ≥48 hours of invasive/noninvasive ventilation; E pulmonary hemorrhage requiring vascular embolization; F SpO2 ≤ Table VIII value twice within a 12-month period ≥30 days apart; or G two qualifying exacerbations/complications (G.1 IV-antibiotic exacerbation, G.2 hemoptysis hospitalization, G.3 enteral/parenteral nutrition ≥90 days, or G.4 CFRD requiring insulin ≥90 days) within a 12-month period.

children.criterion: Cystic Fibrosis documented as described in 3.00J2 (sweat chloride test or CFTR genetic testing)
One of A through G
FEV1 (see 3.00E) less than or equal to the value in Table VII-A or VII-B for age, gender, and height without shoes (see 3.00E3a)

Exacerbations or complications (see 3.00J3) requiring three hospitalizations of any length within a 12-month period and at least 30 days apart (the 12-month period must occur within the period we are considering in connection with your application or continuing disability review)
Spontaneous pneumothorax, secondary to CF, requiring chest tube placement

Respiratory failure (see 3.00N) requiring invasive mechanical ventilation, noninvasive ventilation with BiPAP, or a combination of both treatments, for a continuous period of at least 48 hours, or for a continuous period of at least 72 hours if postoperatively
Pulmonary hemorrhage requiring vascular embolization to control bleeding

SpO2 measured by pulse oximetry (see 3.00H3) either at rest, during a 6MWT, or after a 6MWT, less than or equal to the value in Table VIII, twice within a 12-month period and at least 30 days apart (the 12-month period must occur within the period we are considering in connection with your application or continuing disability review)
Two of the following exacerbations or complications (either two of the same or two different, see 3.00J3 and 3.00J4) within a 12-month period (G.1 through G.4)
Pulmonary exacerbation requiring 10 consecutive days of intravenous antibiotic treatment
Pulmonary hemorrhage (hemoptysis with more than blood-streaked sputum but not requiring vascular embolization) requiring hospitalization of any length
Weight loss requiring daily supplemental enteral nutrition via a gastrostomy for at least 90 consecutive days, or parenteral nutrition via a central venous catheter for at least 90 consecutive days
CFRD requiring daily insulin therapy for at least 90 consecutive days

3.07.title: Bronchiectasis
3.07.summary: Bronchiectasis (see 3.00K), documented by imaging (see 3.00D3), with exacerbations or complications requiring three hospitalizations within a 12-month period and at least 30 days apart. Each hospitalization must last at least 48 hours, including hours in a hospital emergency department immediately before the hospitalization.

children.criterion: Bronchiectasis (see 3.00K), documented by imaging (see 3.00D3), with exacerbations or complications requiring three hospitalizations within a 12-month period and at least 30 days apart. Each hospitalization must last at least 48 hours, including hours in a hospital emergency department immediately before the hospitalization. The 12-month period must occur within the period under consideration.

3.09.title: Chronic pulmonary hypertension due to any cause
3.09.summary: Chronic pulmonary hypertension confirmed by right heart catheterization showing mean pulmonary artery pressure ≥40 mm Hg.

rule_json.criterion: Chronic pulmonary hypertension confirmed by right heart catheterization showing mean pulmonary artery pressure ≥40 mm Hg

3.11.title: Lung transplantation
3.11.summary: Lung transplantation (see 3.00M). Consider under a disability for 3 years from the date of the transplant; after that, evaluate the residual impairment(s).

children.criterion: Lung transplantation (see 3.00M). Consider under a disability for 3 years from the date of the transplant; after that, evaluate the residual impairment(s).

3.14.title: Respiratory failure
3.14.summary: Respiratory failure (see 3.00N) resulting from any underlying chronic respiratory disorder except CF (for CF, see 3.04D), requiring invasive mechanical ventilation, noninvasive ventilation with BiPAP, or a combination of both treatments, for a continuous period of at least 48 hours (or 72 hours if postoperatively), twice within a 12-month period and at least 30 days apart.

children.criterion: Respiratory failure (see 3.00N) resulting from any underlying chronic respiratory disorder except CF (for CF, see 3.04D), requiring invasive mechanical ventilation, noninvasive ventilation with BiPAP, or a combination of both treatments, for a continuous period of at least 48 hours, or for a continuous period of at least 72 hours if postoperatively, twice within a 12-month period and at least 30 days apart. The 12-month period must occur within the period under consideration.

4.02.title: Chronic heart failure
4.02.summary: Chronic heart failure while on prescribed treatment, meeting BOTH A and B. A documents systolic failure (A.1: LVEDD >6.0 cm or EF ≤30% during stability) or diastolic failure (A.2: LV posterior wall + septal thickness ≥2.5 cm with left atrium ≥4.5 cm and normal/elevated EF). B documents one of: B.1 persistent symptoms very seriously limiting ADLs in a patient for whom exercise testing would present significant risk; B.2 three or more episodes of acute CHF within a consecutive 12-month period with fluid retention, requiring hospitalization/ER ≥12 hours; or B.3 inability to perform an exercise tolerance test at a workload ≤5 METs due to B.3.a dyspnea/fatigue/palpitations/chest discomfort, B.3.b VT or ventricular ectopy ≥6/min, B.3.c ≥10 mm Hg systolic BP drop, or B.3.d signs of inadequate cerebral perfusion.

children.criterion: Chronic heart failure while on a regimen of prescribed treatment, with symptoms and signs described in 4.00D2
Medically documented presence of A.1 (systolic failure) or A.2 (diastolic failure)

Systolic failure (see 4.00D1a(i)), with left ventricular end diastolic dimensions greater than 6.0 cm OR ejection fraction of 30 percent or less during a period of stability (not during an episode of acute heart failure)

Diastolic failure (see 4.00D1a(ii)), with left ventricular posterior wall plus septal thickness totaling 2.5 cm or greater on imaging, with an enlarged left atrium ≥4.5 cm, with normal or elevated ejection fraction during a period of stability (not during an episode of acute heart failure)
Resulting in one of B.1, B.2, or B.3

Persistent symptoms of heart failure which very seriously limit the ability to independently initiate, sustain, or complete activities of daily living in an individual for whom an MC, preferably one experienced in the care of patients with cardiovascular disease, has concluded that the performance of an exercise test would present a significant risk to the individual

Three or more separate episodes of acute congestive heart failure within a consecutive 12-month period (see 4.00A3e), with evidence of fluid retention (see 4.00D2b(ii)) from clinical and imaging assessments at the time of the episodes, requiring acute extended physician intervention such as hospitalization or emergency room treatment for 12 hours or more, separated by periods of stabilization (see 4.00D4c)
Inability to perform on an exercise tolerance test at a workload equivalent to 5 METs or less due to one of B.3.a, B.3.b, B.3.c, or B.3.d
Dyspnea, fatigue, palpitations, or chest discomfort
Three or more consecutive premature ventricular contractions (ventricular tachycardia), or increasing frequency of ventricular ectopy with at least 6 premature ventricular contractions per minute

Decrease of 10 mm Hg or more in systolic pressure below the baseline systolic blood pressure or the preceding systolic pressure measured during exercise (see 4.00D4d) due to left ventricular dysfunction, despite an increase in workload
Signs attributable to inadequate cerebral perfusion, such as ataxic gait or mental confusion

4.04.title: Ischemic heart disease
4.04.summary: Ischemic heart disease with symptoms of myocardial ischemia while on prescribed treatment, meeting one of: A sign- or symptom-limited exercise tolerance test at ≤5 METs with A.1 horizontal/downsloping ST depression ≥0.10 mV, A.2 ≥0.1 mV ST elevation in non-infarct leads, A.3 systolic BP drop ≥10 mm Hg from LV dysfunction, or A.4 imaging-documented ischemia at ≤5 METs; B three separate ischemic episodes within a consecutive 12-month period each requiring revascularization or not amenable to revascularization; or C angiographic CAD with significant risk of exercise testing AND both C.1 angiographic criteria (C.1.a-e) and C.2 very serious limitation of ADLs.

children.criterion: Ischemic heart disease, with symptoms due to myocardial ischemia, as described in 4.00E3-4.00E7, while on a regimen of prescribed treatment (see 4.00B3 if there is no regimen of prescribed treatment)
One of A, B, or C
Sign- or symptom-limited exercise tolerance test demonstrating at least one of A.1, A.2, A.3, or A.4 at a workload equivalent to 5 METs or less

Horizontal or downsloping depression, in the absence of digitalis glycoside treatment or hypokalemia, of the ST segment of at least -0.10 millivolts (-1.0 mm) in at least 3 consecutive complexes that are on a level baseline in any lead other than aVR, and depression of at least -0.10 millivolts lasting for at least 1 minute of recovery
At least 0.1 millivolt (1 mm) ST elevation above resting baseline in non-infarct leads during both exercise and 1 or more minutes of recovery

Decrease of 10 mm Hg or more in systolic pressure below the baseline blood pressure or the preceding systolic pressure measured during exercise (see 4.00E9e) due to left ventricular dysfunction, despite an increase in workload
Documented ischemia at an exercise level equivalent to 5 METs or less on appropriate medically acceptable imaging, such as radionuclide perfusion scans or stress echocardiography
Three separate ischemic episodes, each requiring revascularization or not amenable to revascularization (see 4.00E9f), within a consecutive 12-month period (see 4.00A3e)

Coronary artery disease, demonstrated by angiography (obtained independent of Social Security disability evaluation) or other appropriate medically acceptable imaging, and in the absence of a timely exercise tolerance test or a timely normal drug-induced stress test, an MC (preferably one experienced in cardiovascular disease) has concluded that performance of exercise tolerance testing would present a significant risk to the individual, with BOTH C.1 and C.2
Angiographic evidence showing one of C.1.a, C.1.b, C.1.c, C.1.d, or C.1.e
50 percent or more narrowing of a nonbypassed left main coronary artery
70 percent or more narrowing of another nonbypassed coronary artery
50 percent or more narrowing involving a long (greater than 1 cm) segment of a nonbypassed coronary artery
50 percent or more narrowing of at least two nonbypassed coronary arteries
70 percent or more narrowing of a bypass graft vessel
Resulting in very serious limitations in the ability to independently initiate, sustain, or complete activities of daily living

4.05.title: Recurrent arrhythmias
4.05.summary: Recurrent arrhythmias, not related to reversible causes, resulting in uncontrolled recurrent episodes of cardiac syncope or near-syncope despite prescribed treatment, and documented by resting or ambulatory (Holter) electrocardiography or other appropriate testing coincident with the syncopal episodes.

children.criterion: Recurrent arrhythmias, not related to reversible causes such as electrolyte abnormalities or digitalis glycoside or antiarrhythmic drug toxicity, resulting in uncontrolled (see 4.00A3f) recurrent (see 4.00A3c) episodes of cardiac syncope or near-syncope (see 4.00F3b) despite prescribed treatment (see 4.00B3 if no prescribed treatment), and documented by resting or ambulatory (Holter) electrocardiography or by other appropriate medically acceptable testing, coincident with the occurrence of syncope or near-syncope (see 4.00F3c).

4.06.title: Symptomatic congenital heart disease
4.06.summary: Symptomatic congenital heart disease (cyanotic or acyanotic), documented by appropriate medically acceptable imaging (see 4.00A3d) or cardiac catheterization, meeting one of: A cyanosis at rest with A.1 hematocrit ≥55% or A.2 arterial O2 saturation <90% in room air or resting PaO2 ≤60 Torr; B intermittent right-to-left shunting resulting in cyanosis on exertion (e.g., Eisenmenger's physiology) with arterial PaO2 ≤60 Torr at a workload ≤5 METs; or C secondary pulmonary vascular obstructive disease with pulmonary arterial systolic pressure ≥70% of the systemic arterial systolic pressure.

children.criterion: Symptomatic congenital heart disease (cyanotic or acyanotic), documented by appropriate medically acceptable imaging (see 4.00A3d) or cardiac catheterization
One of A, B, or C
Cyanosis at rest, AND one of A.1 or A.2
Cyanosis at rest
A.1 or A.2
Hematocrit of 55 percent or greater
Arterial O2 saturation of less than 90 percent in room air, OR resting arterial PO2 of 60 Torr or less
Intermittent right-to-left shunting resulting in cyanosis on exertion (e.g., Eisenmenger's physiology) and with arterial PO2 of 60 Torr or less at a workload equivalent to 5 METs or less
Secondary pulmonary vascular obstructive disease with pulmonary arterial systolic pressure elevated to at least 70 percent of the systemic arterial systolic pressure

4.09.title: Heart transplant
4.09.summary: Heart transplant. Consider under a disability for 1 year following surgery; thereafter, evaluate residual impairment under the appropriate listing.

children.criterion: Heart transplant. Consider under a disability for 1 year following surgery; thereafter, evaluate residual impairment under the appropriate listing.

4.10.title: Aneurysm of aorta or major branches
4.10.summary: Aneurysm of aorta or major branches, due to any cause, demonstrated by appropriate medically acceptable imaging, with dissection not controlled by prescribed treatment (see 4.00H6).

children.criterion: Aneurysm of aorta or major branches, due to any cause (e.g., atherosclerosis, cystic medial necrosis, Marfan syndrome, trauma), demonstrated by appropriate medically acceptable imaging, with dissection not controlled by prescribed treatment (see 4.00H6). Dissection is not controlled when there is persistence of chest pain due to progression of the dissection, an increase in aneurysm size, or compression of one or more aortic branches supplying the heart, kidneys, brain, or other organs.

4.11.title: Chronic venous insufficiency
4.11.summary: Chronic venous insufficiency of a lower extremity with extensive brawny edema or superficial varicosities, stasis dermatitis, and recurrent or persistent ulceration not healing after 3 months of prescribed treatment.

children.criterion: Chronic venous insufficiency of a lower extremity with deep venous thrombosis, valvular incompetence, or post-thrombotic syndrome

Extensive brawny edema involving at least two-thirds of the leg between ankle and knee, OR superficial varicosities, stasis dermatitis, AND recurrent or persistent ulceration that has not healed after at least 3 months of prescribed treatment

4.12.title: Peripheral arterial disease
4.12.summary: Peripheral arterial disease (as determined by appropriate medically acceptable imaging per 4.00A3d, 4.00G2, 4.00G5, 4.00G6) causing intermittent claudication (see 4.00G1), meeting one of: A resting ankle/brachial systolic blood pressure ratio less than 0.50; B decrease in systolic blood pressure at the ankle on exercise of 50% or more of pre-exercise level requiring ≥10 minutes to return to pre-exercise level (see 4.00G7a, 4.00C16-4.00C17); C resting toe systolic pressure less than 30 mm Hg (see 4.00G7c, 4.00G8); or D resting toe/brachial systolic blood pressure ratio less than 0.40 (see 4.00G7c).

children.criterion: Peripheral arterial disease, as determined by appropriate medically acceptable imaging (see 4.00A3d, 4.00G2, 4.00G5, and 4.00G6), causing intermittent claudication (see 4.00G1)
One of A, B, C, or D
Resting ankle/brachial systolic blood pressure ratio of less than 0.50

Decrease in systolic blood pressure at the ankle on exercise (see 4.00G7a and 4.00C16-4.00C17) of 50 percent or more of pre-exercise level and requiring 10 minutes or more to return to pre-exercise level
Resting toe systolic pressure of less than 30 mm Hg (see 4.00G7c and 4.00G8)
Resting toe/brachial systolic blood pressure ratio of less than 0.40 (see 4.00G7c)

5.02.title: Gastrointestinal hemorrhaging from any cause
5.02.summary: Gastrointestinal hemorrhaging from any cause, requiring blood transfusion of at least 2 units per transfusion, occurring at least three times during a consecutive 6-month period (transfusions at least 30 days apart). Consider under a disability for 1 year following the last documented transfusion; thereafter, evaluate the residual impairment(s).

children.criterion: Gastrointestinal hemorrhaging from any cause, requiring blood transfusion (with or without hospitalization) of at least 2 units of blood per transfusion, and occurring at least three times during a consecutive 6-month period. The transfusions must be at least 30 days apart within the 6-month period. Consider under a disability for 1 year following the last documented transfusion; thereafter, evaluate the residual impairment(s).

5.05.title: Chronic liver disease
5.05.summary: Chronic liver disease meeting one of: A hemorrhaging from varices/portal hypertensive gastropathy causing hemodynamic instability requiring transfusion of ≥2 units (12-month presumptive disability post-transfusion); B ascites or hydrothorax despite prescribed treatment on at least two evaluations ≥60 days apart within a consecutive 6-month period; C spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (ANC ≥250 cells/mm3); D hepatorenal syndrome with D.1 serum creatinine ≥2 mg/dL, D.2 oliguria (24h urine <500 mL), or D.3 sodium retention (urine sodium <10 mEq/L); E hepatopulmonary syndrome; F hepatic encephalopathy; or G end-stage liver disease with SSA CLD scores ≥22.

children.criterion: Hemorrhaging from esophageal, gastric, or ectopic varices or from portal hypertensive gastropathy, demonstrated by endoscopy, x-ray, or other appropriate medically acceptable imaging, resulting in hemodynamic instability as defined in 5.00D5, and requiring hospitalization for transfusion of at least 2 units of blood. Consider under a disability for 1 year following the last documented transfusion; thereafter, evaluate the residual impairment(s).

Ascites or hydrothorax not attributable to other causes, despite continuing treatment as prescribed, present on at least two evaluations at least 60 days apart within a consecutive 6-month period. Each evaluation must be documented by laboratory and clinical findings.
Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis with peritoneal fluid containing an absolute neutrophil count of at least 250 cells/mm3
Hepatorenal syndrome as described in 5.00D8, with one of D.1, D.2, or D.3
Serum creatinine elevation of at least 2 mg/dL
Oliguria with 24-hour urine output less than 500 mL
Sodium retention with urine sodium less than 10 mEq per liter
Hepatopulmonary syndrome as described in 5.00D9 (arterial hypoxemia with intrapulmonary vascular dilatations)
Hepatic encephalopathy as described in 5.00D10, with documented altered mental status, signs of asterixis or other neurologic findings, and either elevated ammonia or EEG abnormalities
End stage liver disease with SSA CLD scores of 22 or greater calculated as described in 5.00D11. Consider under a disability from at least the date of the first score.

5.06.title: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)
5.06.summary: Inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn's or ulcerative colitis) with obstruction requiring hospitalization, OR two of the following within 6 months: anemia, low albumin, tender abdominal mass, perineal disease, weight loss, or dependence on supplemental daily nutrition.

children.criterion: Obstruction of stenotic areas (not adhesions) in small intestine or colon with proximal dilation, confirmed by imaging or in surgery, requiring hospitalization for intestinal decompression or surgery on two occasions within consecutive 6-month period
Two of the following despite continuing treatment, present on at least two evaluations at least 60 days apart within a 6-month period
At least two of the listed symptoms
Anemia with hemoglobin <10.0 g/dL
Serum albumin ≤3.0 g/dL
Clinically documented tender abdominal mass with abdominal pain or cramping not controlled by prescribed narcotic medication
Perineal disease with draining abscess or fistula with pain
Involuntary weight loss of at least 10% from baseline
Need for supplemental daily enteral nutrition via gastrostomy or daily parenteral nutrition via central venous catheter
On at least two evaluations 60 days apart in 6-month period

5.07.title: Short bowel syndrome (SBS)
5.07.summary: Short bowel syndrome (SBS), due to surgical resection of more than one-half of the small intestine, with dependence on daily parenteral nutrition via a central venous catheter (see 5.00F).

children.criterion: Short bowel syndrome (SBS), due to surgical resection of more than one-half of the small intestine, with dependence on daily parenteral nutrition via a central venous catheter (see 5.00F).

5.08.title: Weight loss due to any digestive disorder
5.08.summary: Weight loss due to any digestive disorder despite continuing treatment as prescribed, with BMI of less than 17.50 calculated on at least two evaluations at least 60 days apart within a consecutive 6-month period.

children.criterion: Weight loss due to any digestive disorder despite continuing treatment as prescribed, with BMI of less than 17.50 calculated on at least two evaluations at least 60 days apart within a consecutive 6-month period.

5.09.title: Liver transplantation
5.09.summary: Liver transplantation. Consider under a disability for 1 year following the date of transplantation; thereafter, evaluate the residual impairment(s) (see 5.00D12 and 5.00H).

children.criterion: Liver transplantation. Consider under a disability for 1 year following the date of transplantation; thereafter, evaluate the residual impairment(s) (see 5.00D12 and 5.00H).

5.11.title: Small intestine transplantation
5.11.summary: Small intestine transplantation; considered disabled for 1 year from the date of transplant, after which residual impairment is evaluated.

children.criterion: Small intestine transplantation documented by operative report or transplant center records
Within 1 year of transplant date (claimant considered disabled for 1 year post-transplant)

5.12.title: Pancreas transplantation
5.12.summary: Pancreas transplantation; considered disabled for 1 year from the date of transplant, after which residual impairment is evaluated.

children.criterion: Pancreas transplantation documented by operative report or transplant center records
Within 1 year of transplant date (claimant considered disabled for 1 year post-transplant)

6.03.title: Chronic kidney disease with chronic hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis
6.03.summary: Chronic kidney disease with chronic hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis (see 6.00C1). Ongoing dialysis must have lasted or be expected to last for a continuous period of at least 12 months.

children.criterion: Chronic kidney disease with chronic hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis (see 6.00C1). Ongoing dialysis must have lasted or be expected to last for a continuous period of at least 12 months. Either modality (hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis) satisfies the listing.

6.04.title: Chronic kidney disease with kidney transplant
6.04.summary: Chronic kidney disease with kidney transplant. Consider under a disability for 1 year following the transplant; thereafter, evaluate the residual impairment (see 6.00C2).

children.criterion: Chronic kidney disease with kidney transplant. Consider under a disability for 1 year following the transplant; thereafter, evaluate the residual impairment (see 6.00C2).

6.05.title: Chronic kidney disease with impairment of kidney function
6.05.summary: Chronic kidney disease with both: (A) reduced glomerular filtration evidenced by elevated serum creatinine, low creatinine clearance, or low eGFR on at least two occasions 90+ days apart within 12 months, AND (B) one of four complications: renal osteodystrophy with bone pain + imaging, peripheral neuropathy, fluid overload syndrome, or anorexia with BMI <=18.0.

children.criterion: Reduced glomerular filtration: one of three lab findings on at least two occasions at least 90 days apart within a consecutive 12-month period
Serum creatinine of 4 mg/dL or greater
Creatinine clearance of 20 mL/min or less
Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 20 mL/min/1.73m^2 or less
One of four complications of CKD
Renal osteodystrophy with severe bone pain AND imaging studies documenting bone abnormalities (osteitis fibrosa, osteomalacia, or pathologic fractures)
Peripheral neuropathy (uremic or other)
Fluid overload syndrome documented by one of two findings
Diastolic hypertension >=110 mmHg despite at least 90 consecutive days of prescribed therapy, documented by at least two measurements at least 90 days apart within a 12-month period
Signs of vascular congestion or anasarca despite at least 90 consecutive days of prescribed therapy, documented on at least two occasions at least 90 days apart within a 12-month period
Anorexia with weight loss determined by body mass index (BMI) of 18.0 or less, calculated on at least two occasions at least 90 days apart within a 12-month period

6.06.title: Nephrotic syndrome
6.06.summary: Nephrotic syndrome with laboratory findings of heavy proteinuria (either >=10 g/24h OR >=3.5 g/24h with low serum albumin), AND anasarca persisting at least 90 days despite prescribed treatment.

children.criterion: Laboratory findings supporting nephrotic syndrome, documented on at least two occasions >=90 days apart within a 12-month period
Proteinuria of 10.0 g or greater per 24 hours
Serum albumin <=3.0 g/dL with proteinuria >=3.5 g/24h or UPCR >=3.5
Serum albumin of 3.0 g/dL or less
Heavy urinary protein loss
Proteinuria of 3.5 g or greater per 24 hours
Urine total-protein-to-creatinine ratio of 3.5 or greater
Anasarca persisting for at least 90 days despite prescribed treatment

6.09.title: Complications of chronic kidney disease
6.09.summary: Complications of chronic kidney disease (see 6.00C8) requiring at least three hospitalizations within a consecutive 12-month period and occurring at least 30 days apart. Each hospitalization must last at least 48 hours, including hours in a hospital emergency department immediately before the hospitalization.

children.criterion: Complications of chronic kidney disease (see 6.00C8) requiring at least three hospitalizations within a consecutive 12-month period and occurring at least 30 days apart. Each hospitalization must last at least 48 hours, including hours in a hospital emergency department immediately before the hospitalization. The hospitalizations may be for different complications of CKD (e.g., stroke, congestive heart failure, hypertensive crisis, acute kidney failure requiring a short course of hemodialysis).

7.05.title: Hemolytic anemias, including sickle cell disease, thalassemia, and their variants
7.05.summary: Hemolytic anemia (sickle cell disease, thalassemia, etc.) with documented severe complications (vaso-occlusive crises, transfusion needs, hemolytic crises) occurring at specified frequency within 12-month period.

children.criterion: Documented painful (vaso-occlusive) crises requiring parenteral narcotic medication occurring at least 6 times within 12-month period, with at least 30 days between crises
Hospital complications occurring at least 3 times within 12-month period (hospital admission lasting ≥48 hours; each at least 30 days apart)
Chronic, severe anemia with hemoglobin ≤7.0 g/dL on at least 3 evaluations at least 30 days apart within 12-month period
Beta thalassemia major requiring life-long red blood cell transfusions at least once every 6 weeks to maintain Hgb

7.08.title: Disorders of thrombosis and hemostasis
7.08.summary: Disorders of thrombosis and hemostasis, including hemophilia and thrombocytopenia (see 7.00D), with complications requiring at least three hospitalizations within a 12-month period and occurring at least 30 days apart. Each hospitalization must last at least 48 hours, which can include hours in a hospital emergency department or comprehensive hemophilia treatment center immediately before the hospitalization (see 7.00D2).

children.criterion: Disorders of thrombosis and hemostasis, including hemophilia and thrombocytopenia (see 7.00D), with complications requiring at least three hospitalizations within a 12-month period and occurring at least 30 days apart. Each hospitalization must last at least 48 hours, which can include hours in a hospital emergency department or comprehensive hemophilia treatment center immediately before the hospitalization (see 7.00D2).

7.10.title: Disorders of bone marrow failure
7.10.summary: Bone marrow failure (aplastic anemia, myelodysplastic syndrome, etc.) with severe infection or bleeding requiring hospitalizations, OR transfusion-dependence, OR severe cytopenias.

children.criterion: Hospitalization for complications (severe infection or hemorrhage) requiring ≥48-hour hospitalization, occurring at least three times within 12-month period
Transfusion-dependent severe anemia (Hgb ≤7.0) on at least 3 occasions in 12 months, OR thrombocytopenia (PLT ≤30,000) on at least 3 evaluations 30+ days apart in 12 months

7.17.title: Hematological disorders treated by bone marrow or stem cell transplantation
7.17.summary: Hematological disorders treated by bone marrow or stem cell transplantation (see 7.00F). Consider under a disability for at least 12 consecutive months from the date of transplantation. After that, evaluate any residual impairment(s) under the criteria for the affected body system.

children.criterion: Hematological disorders treated by bone marrow or stem cell transplantation (see 7.00F). Consider under a disability for at least 12 consecutive months from the date of transplantation. After that, evaluate any residual impairment(s) under the criteria for the affected body system.

7.18.title: Repeated complications of hematological disorders
7.18.summary: Hematological disorder with repeated complications resulting in significant interference with ADLs, social functioning, or completing tasks in timely manner due to deficiencies in concentration/persistence/pace.

Marked limitation in completing tasks in timely manner due to concentration, persistence, or pace deficiencies

8.03.title: Bullous disease
8.03.summary: Bullous disease (e.g., pemphigus, erythema multiforme bullosum, epidermolysis bullosa, bullous pemphigoid, dermatitis herpetiformis), with extensive skin lesions that persist for at least 3 months despite continuing treatment as prescribed.

8.04.title: Chronic infections of the skin or mucous membranes
8.04.summary: Chronic infections of the skin or mucous membranes, with extensive fungating or extensive ulcerating skin lesions that persist for at least 3 months despite continuing treatment as prescribed.

children.criterion: Chronic infection of skin or mucous membranes, with extensive fungating or extensive ulcerating skin lesions that persist for at least 3 months despite continuing treatment as prescribed

8.05.title: Dermatitis
8.05.summary: Dermatitis (e.g., psoriasis, dyshidrosis, atopic dermatitis, exfoliative dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis), with extensive skin lesions that persist for at least 3 months despite continuing treatment as prescribed.

children.criterion: Dermatitis diagnosis (psoriasis, dyshidrosis, atopic dermatitis, exfoliative dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, etc.), with extensive skin lesions persisting for at least 3 months despite continuing treatment as prescribed

8.06.title: Hidradenitis suppurativa
8.06.summary: Hidradenitis suppurativa, with extensive skin lesions involving both axillae, both inguinal areas, or the perineum, that persist for at least 3 months despite continuing treatment as prescribed.

children.criterion: Hidradenitis suppurativa diagnosis, with extensive skin lesions involving both axillae, both inguinal areas, or the perineum, persisting for at least 3 months despite continuing treatment as prescribed

Extensive skin lesions involving both inguinal areas
